subject: Operational runbook and evidence orchestration for international transfer questions
messages:
From: Allen Pierce <allen.pierce@medixcorp.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: MedixCorp Legal Team <legal@medixcorp.com>
Date: Tue, 01 May 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Clarify transfer safeguards + sample evidence for EU/UK subprocessor set

Diego —

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Legal here is preparing the DPA Annex and we need a narrow evidence package to close our TIA gating items. Specifically MedixCorp needs:

- A mapping (by subprocessor) showing which processing occurs in EU vs UK vs US and the contractual mechanism used (SCCs vs UK IDTA/UK addendum).
- Samples of transit logs (pseudonymized) demonstrating routing to our preferred onshore fallback for European-origin requests.
- Confirmation of whether any caching or batching at edge nodes could result in EU-origin data being processed outside the SCC/IDTA scope (short explanation is fine).
- A list of subprocessors with the date they were added and current attestations (SaaS subprocessors only).

Can you provide a short operational runbook for the evidence handoff (who will upload what, expected formats, and a target signoff date)? We are hoping to have the TIA cleared by 2028-05-12.

Appreciate concise answers and any attachments you can share.

—Allen
Allen Pierce
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
MedixCorp

[Attachment: initial-question-list.txt]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Allen Pierce <allen.pierce@medixcorp.com>
Cc: MedixCorp Legal Team <legal@medixcorp.com>
Date: Tue, 01 May 2028 14:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify transfer safeguards + sample evidence for EU/UK subprocessor set

Allen —

Thanks, this is a clear ask. High level answers below; we will provide the runbook and artifacts as attachments by EOD Friday (2028-05-05).

- Mapping: attached is a draft mapping (redwood-tia-mapping.xlsx) with subprocessor, region, mechanism column. We will add column-level notes for any multi-region processors.
- Transit logs: we can provide pseudonymized request-routing logs showing source country and final compute region. Expect a CSV sample (10k rows) with hashed identifiers.
- Caching/batching: short answer — our edge prefix cache may store KV entries at regional PoPs for up to 6 hours; those caches only contain model prompt prefixes and not long-term customer data. We will include a 2-paragraph technical note with the runbook.
- Subprocessors: attached is the latest subprocessors export (we will include dates and attestations).

Proposed runbook (summary):
1) Redwood: compile artifacts into a Drive folder (redwood evidence pack). Owner: Diego (runbook owner).
2) Internal review: Kim (kimberly_park) validates attestations; Jonas (jonas_weber) validates routing logs sampling methodology.
3) Upload: Naomi (naomi_feldman) will upload final artifacts to MedixCorp shared folder and notify legal.
4) Signoff: target signoff by MedixCorp legal on/around 2028-05-12.

Attaching the draft mapping and a short SCCs/UK-addendum summary.

If that timeline works, we will kick off an internal sprint tomorrow.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Manager, Privacy Partnerships
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: redwood-tia-mapping.xlsx, sccs-uk-addendum-summary.pdf]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 May 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: sprint to assemble MedixCorp evidence pack (TIA) — action items

Team —

Allen asked for a compact evidence handoff with a Friday delivery. I outlined a minimal runbook in my reply; we need to move fast. Actions below (please reply in-thread with ETA):

Kimberly (kimberly_park) — validate subprocessors sheet for legal posture. Check each SaaS processor row for: contract mechanism flagged, date_added, and attestation file link. Flag any stale attestations (older than 12 months). Expected deliverable: annotated CSV + list of 1-3 processors requiring re-attestation.

Jonas (jonas_weber) — prepare a 2-page technical note on caching/batching behavior (include TTLs, how prefix caching is scoped to PoPs, and whether any KV persistence exists beyond 24 hours). Also prepare a pseudonymized sample of routing logs (CSV) with schema and hash salt explanation. Deliverable: technical_note.pdf + routing_sample.csv (10k rows).

Naomi (naomi_feldman) — coordinate the Drive folder and upload final artifacts. Make sure access is set to the MedixCorp shared folder and generate a download audit link. Deliverable: drive_link + evidence index doc (evidence-hand-off-checklist.docx).

I'll collect and stitch together Friday morning for a clean package to send. If anything looks like it will be delayed, flag immediately.

Diego

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Allen Pierce <allen.pierce@medixcorp.com>
Cc: MedixCorp Legal Team <legal@medixcorp.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 May 2028 16:45:00 -0400
Subject: Evidence pack and runbook for MedixCorp TIA — deliverable (attachments + notes)

Allen / MedixCorp legal —

Please find attached the evidence pack we discussed. Summary of contents and short clarifications below. If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough next week.

Attachments included:
- redwood-tia-mapping.xlsx — subprocessor by region, contractual mechanism (SCCs or UK Addendum), date_added, attestation link.
- routing_sample.csv — pseudonymized routing sample (10,000 rows). Column note included in technical_note.pdf.
- technical_note.pdf — short explanations on caching, batching, and PoP scoping. Key point: prefix KV caches are regional PoP-scoped, TTL max 6 hours, no long-term persistence beyond 24 hours for any request metadata.
- evidence-hand-off-checklist.docx — index of delivered artifacts and internal owners.
- sccs-uk-addendum-summary.pdf — legal summary of our use of SCCs and applicability of the UK addendum for UK-origin requests.

Quick answers to your bullets:
- Mapping: included and annotated. Any multi-region processors are flagged in column G.
- Transit logs: routing_sample.csv demonstrates source_country -> edge_pop -> compute_region. All user-identifiable fields hashed. We used salt hash SHA256 with a per-run random salt (description in technical_note.pdf).
- Caching/batching risk: technical_note.pdf addresses this — short answer is that occasional edge caching does not change the contractual mechanism because the compute region for the final model execution is enforced by routing policy (SCC/IDTA mapping applies to compute region).
- Subprocessors & attestations: see mapping; three processors (listed in the mapping) require updated attestations — we have initiated re-attestation and expect them within 10 business days.

Runbook (detailed steps are in the checklist):
1) Redwood prepares artifacts (completed). Owner: Diego.
2) Redwood internal validation (completed). Owners: Kimberly, Jonas.
3) Upload to MedixCorp controlled folder and share link (completed). Uploader: Naomi. Folder link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_sprint-evidence-pack.
4) MedixCorp legal reviews and either confirms TIA clearance or requests follow-ups by 2028-05-12.

Next steps: let me know if you'd like the walkthrough; otherwise we consider this package the official artifact for the current SOW/TIA review.

Best regards,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Manager, Privacy Partnerships
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: redwood-tia-mapping.xlsx, routing_sample.csv, technical_note.pdf, evidence-hand-off-checklist.docx, sccs-uk-addendum-summary.pdf]
